raw_case_text:
A 38 Year old female patient, resident of district Gonda, Uttar Pradesh presented with the chief complaints of a painless swelling in the left axillary region for the past 5 months. She had no history of fever, cough, weight loss, or any other swelling elsewhere in the body.
Local examination revealed a nontender mass with limited mobility measuring 3 cm x 2 cm with heterogeneous (soft to firm) consistency [Figure 1a]. General examination revealed the absence of palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy.
A provisional diagnosis of tubercular axillary lymphadenitis was considered. Ultrasonography revealed a well-defined ovoid solid mass in the left axilla measuring 50 mm x 22 mm with echogenic core [Figure 1b]. Morever, small cystic area was seen along posterior surface measuring 24 mm x 13 mm. A radiological diagnosis of large reactionary lymphadenitis was made.
Fine-needle aspiration from the swelling was performed and yielded 9 ml of hemorrhagic fluid. The smears revealed multiple sheathed, coiled, slightly curved mf of bancrofti with the prominence of lymphocytes along with the presence of few eosinophils in a proteinaceous background [Figures 2a and b]. On FNAC, a diagnosis of filarial parasitic infestation was made. Complete blood count revealed eosinophilia (15%) with absolute eosinophil count of 1680/mul of the blood. Peripheral blood smear examination did not reveal microfilaria. The patient was started on diethylcarbamazine citrate, and on follow-up, the swelling reduced.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old Indian female presenting with a 5-month history of a painless left axillary swelling.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a solitary, painless swelling in the left axilla noticed 5 months prior to consultation, without constitutional symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of Gonda district, Uttar Pradesh, India (filariasis-endemic region).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for painless left axillary mass; negative for fever, cough, weight loss, or swellings elsewhere.

objective.physical_examination: Local examination revealed a non-tender, soft-to-firm left axillary mass measuring 3 x 2 cm with restricted mobility and no generalized peripheral lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC demonstrated peripheral eosinophilia (15%, absolute eosinophil count 1,680/uL), while peripheral blood smear was negative for microfilariae. Axillary ultrasonography showed a well-defined 50 x 22 mm ovoid solid mass with an echogenic core and a 24 x 13 mm posterior cystic component.
objective.advanced_workup: Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the left axillary swelling yielded 9 mL of hemorrhagic fluid; cytological smears demonstrated numerous sheathed, coiled Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae alongside lymphocytes and eosinophils in a proteinaceous background.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Confirmed isolated axillary lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti), established by FNAC demonstration of sheathed microfilariae.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with oral diethylcarbamazine citrate (DEC), resulting in marked regression of the axillary swelling on follow-up.
